bmt-2015-geometry-tiebreaker-01.title: Affine coordinates
bmt-2015-geometry-tiebreaker-01.body:
Ratios along lines are preserved by affine maps, so take $A=(0,0)$, $B=(1,0)$, $D=(0,1)$, $C=(1,1)$ (so $AB$ corresponds to length $7$). Then $DC$ has length $7$ and $E$ is $91$ beyond $C$: $E=(1+\frac{91}{7},1)=(14,1)$.

$AE$: $y=\frac x{14}$; $BD$: $x+y=1$; they meet at $X=\left(\frac{14}{15},\frac1{15}\right)$. Line $CX$ has direction $C-X=\left(\frac1{15},\frac{14}{15}\right)\propto(1,14)$; from $C=(1,1)$ it reaches $y=0$ at $x=1-\frac1{14}=\frac{13}{14}$. So $F=\left(\frac{13}{14},0\right)$ and $\frac{AF}{FB}=\frac{13/14}{1/14}=13$.

**Answer: 13**

bmt-2015-geometry-tiebreaker-02.title: Distance from the center to line CE
bmt-2015-geometry-tiebreaker-02.body:
Put $A=(0,0)$, $B=(1,0)$, $C=(1,1)$, $D=(0,1)$, $E=(0,\frac12)$. A circle tangent to $AB$ ($y=0$) and $BC$ ($x=1$) inside the square has center $(1-r,r)$. Line $CE$: $x-2y+1=0$. The distance from the center is $\frac{|2-3r|}{\sqrt5}=r$, so $2-3r=\pm\sqrt5r$. The circle must fit in the square, so $r<1$: $r=\frac{2}{3+\sqrt5}=\frac{3-\sqrt5}{2}\approx0.38$.

**Answer: $\frac{3-\sqrt5}{2}$**

bmt-2015-geometry-tiebreaker-03.title: Use the symmetry axis
bmt-2015-geometry-tiebreaker-03.body:
All six points lie in the plane $x+y+z=6$ and form a hexagon centered at $(2,2,2)$. By symmetry the largest sphere has its center $(t,t,t)$ on the axis through the origin and $(2,2,2)$, and touches the base plane and the lateral faces.

Base plane $x+y+z=6$: distance from $(t,t,t)$ is $\frac{6-3t}{\sqrt3}$.

A lateral face through the origin, $(1,2,3)$ and $(1,3,2)$: the normal is $(1,2,3)\times(1,3,2)=(-5,1,1)$, so the plane is $-5x+y+z=0$ and the distance from $(t,t,t)$ is $\frac{|{-5t}+2t|}{\sqrt{27}}=\frac{t}{\sqrt3}$. (The other five lateral faces are equivalent by symmetry.)

Setting the distances equal: $6-3t=t$, so $t=\frac32$ and $r=\frac{t}{\sqrt3}=\frac{\sqrt3}{2}$.

**Answer: $\frac{\sqrt3}2$**
